Home.title: SquadCrm — AI-first support that knows when to bring in a human
Home.tagline: SquadCrm answers live chat with AI first and hands off to a human agent the moment it's needed. Tickets are answered by a human and delivered by email — admins see every conversation and every SLA in one place.

Hero.headlineLead: Every conversation starts with AI. The hard ones reach a person
Hero.headlineEmphasis: before your customer has to ask twice.
Hero.sub: SquadCrm answers live chat with an AI agent first and hands off to a human the moment it's out of depth. Tickets go straight to a person and land back in your customer's inbox. Admins see every conversation, every SLA, in one place — nothing waits in a shared mailbox.
Hero.note: Escalates automatically at 75% of the SLA target — the same rule you can see live in the preview.
Hero.meta2: Arabic & English, right out of the box
Hero.chatMsg1: I can see your last two orders — which one is the late delivery about?
Hero.chatMsg2: Hi, I've got the full order history in front of me — let's sort this out.
Hero.toast: TKT-2481 escalated to Sara · just now

Problem.heading: The gap isn't answering — it's everything around the answer.
Problem.lead: Most support tools are good at one channel and blind to the rest. The cost shows up as silence, not errors — a customer who quietly gives up is indistinguishable, in most dashboards, from one who was helped.
Problem.item1Body: A customer opens a chat and waits for whoever's free. If no one's free, they wait for nothing — and try again by email.
Problem.item2Body: A chat becomes a ticket, a ticket becomes an email thread — and the next person to answer starts from zero.
Problem.item3Body: Without a shared view of what's overdue, an SLA breach is usually discovered by the customer complaining about it first.

Solution.heading: One system, two ways in, no dropped context.
Solution.para1: Live chat is answered by an AI agent first — built on Gemini, reading the same conversation history a human would. It resolves what it can on the spot.
Solution.para2: The instant a question needs judgment, account access, or an apology a script can't give, it escalates to the team — same thread, same customer, no re-explaining.
Solution.para3: For anything written rather than live — a complaint, a document, a slower issue — customers submit a ticket. A human agent answers it, and the reply is delivered by email, whether or not the customer ever logs back in.
Solution.para4: Every message, ticket, and handoff is logged against one customer record — visible to admins the moment it happens, not after a report is run.
Solution.step1Body: Reads context, resolves straightforward requests immediately.
Solution.step2Body: Same thread. The agent sees everything the AI already gathered.
Solution.step3Body: The customer gets the answer whether or not they're online.

Product.heading: The same record, from three different chairs.
Product.sub: A customer's ticket, an agent's queue, an admin's oversight view — all reading the same underlying case.
Product.ticketDetailCustomerLine: Customer, 09:14 — "Still hasn't shown up on my card, it's been 6 days."
Product.ticketDetailAgentLine: Sara (Agent), 09:41 — "Checked with billing, refund reissued — confirmation below."

Workflow.heading: What actually happens between "I have a problem" and "resolved."
Workflow.step1Body: Customer creates an account, in Arabic or English.
Workflow.step2Body: Opens live chat, or writes up a ticket.
Workflow.step3Body: Gemini answers chat first, drafts reply suggestions for tickets.
Workflow.step4Body: Auto-assigned to a team member, full context carried over.
Workflow.step5Body: Agent replies; ticket reply also goes out by email.
Workflow.step6Body: SLA, CSAT and full history land on the admin's dashboard.

Value.kicker: Built for three people, not one

Bilingual.heading: Arabic and English, including the direction the page reads in.
Bilingual.body: Every screen — the chat widget, the ticket form, the agent workspace — is written through a translation layer from the first line of code, not retrofitted. Switching languages mirrors the entire layout, not just the words.
